correctness.rationale: Restrict the ellipsoid support function to viewing plane: shadow squared semiaxes are eigenvalues of Q=diag(B+η,B,B−Δ) compressed to N⊥. Its 2×2 discriminant is exactly G²=(η−(η+Δ)x²−Δ y²)²+4ηΔ y². We independently assembled the 2×2 compression at six nonpolar normals/two parameter sets and matched this formula to numerical precision. G<tη implies transverse x,y=O(sqrt(η/Δ)); scaled u,v satisfy |1−(u+iv)²|²<t² in the limit. A bounded local chart and algebraic zero-area boundary permit dominated convergence even at t=1; the two hemisphere charts give factor 1/(2π). The branched map w=z² has Jacobian area conversion |C_t|=(1/2)∫_{|w−1|<t}|w|^(−1)dA; polar integration yields the stated E,K formulas, Φ(1)=1/π and Φ small/large limits. Differentiating K as k↑1 yields logarithmic slope coefficient 1/(2π). The open two lobes meet only at boundary at t=1, so the statement correctly distinguishes open from closed connectivity.
